title: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 — Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE): Product quality model
use: Treat software quality as multidimensional rather than a single simplicity/quality score.
caveat: Public abstract supports model-level claims; full normative text is not reproduced here.

title: SEI — Reasoning About Software Quality Attributes
use: Architecture decisions should be reasoned about through concrete quality-attribute scenarios.
caveat: Foundational architecture guidance; implementation mechanisms still depend on project context.

title: SEI — Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method
use: Quality attributes can conflict; architecture involves explicit tradeoffs.
caveat: Koda should borrow the reasoning principle, not reproduce enterprise ATAM ceremony.

title: SEI — Maintainability
use: Maintainability should be considered as a requirement/architectural concern.
caveat: Architecture-level guidance.

title: SEI — Modifiability Tactics
use: Supports reasoning about change cost and structural boundaries.
caveat: Do not automatically apply every tactic or turn them into mandatory patterns.

title: Google Engineering Practices — What to look for in a code review
use: Review design, functionality, complexity, tests, naming, comments/documentation, and maintainability.
caveat: Google-specific process details are not universal.

title: Google Engineering Practices — The standard of code review
use: Improve code health rather than block all progress until theoretical perfection.
caveat: Risk-critical systems may have higher required acceptance standards.

title: Google Engineering Practices — Small CLs
use: Small, focused, self-contained changes improve reviewability and integration.
caveat: There is no universal line-count threshold; some coherent changes are necessarily large.

title: Google Go Style Guide — Style principles
use: Code should be optimized for readers; abstractions should map to the problem and justify their cost.
caveat: Examples are Go-specific; project conventions win.

title: Google TypeScript Style Guide
use: Descriptive names and meaningful interface naming.
caveat: Google-specific conventions are not universal.

title: Google Documentation Best Practices
use: Prefer minimum viable, accurate documentation and update it with code.
caveat: Regulated/public API contexts may require more extensive documentation.

title: DORA — Test automation
use: Fast, reliable automated feedback is valuable; manual exploratory/usability testing still has a role.
caveat: Not every recommendation on the page should become a universal Koda mandate.

title: Google Testing Blog — How Much Testing is Enough?
use: Testing depth depends on software purpose/audience; integration and critical-user-flow testing matter.
caveat: Heuristics are practitioner guidance rather than formal standard.

title: Google Testing Blog — Code Coverage Best Practices
use: Coverage is a gap/risk signal rather than a universal quality score.
caveat: Do not promote Google-specific numeric heuristics into universal gates.

title: Microsoft .NET — Unit testing best practices
use: Good unit tests are fast/repeatable/isolated; high coverage alone does not establish quality.
caveat: .NET examples; general principles are broader.

title: Google Research / ICSE — Long Term Effects of Mutation Testing
use: Mutation testing can reveal meaningful test gaps and correlate with real faults.
caveat: Cost/process overhead makes it selective rather than universal.

title: NIST SP 800-218 — Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) 1.1
use: Security practices should be integrated into software development rather than bolted on later.
caveat: High-level framework; implementation is context-dependent.

title: NIST IR 8397 — Guidelines on Minimum Standards for Developer Verification of Software
use: Threat modeling, automated tests, static scanning, secret detection, built-in protections, black-box/structural/historical tests, fuzzing, web scanning when applicable, and dependency review.
caveat: The document itself says it does not cover the totality of verification; techniques still require applicability judgment.

title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS) 5.0.0
use: Provides testable web security requirements.
caveat: Web-focused; do not apply wholesale to local scripts/desktop-only software.

title: OWASP Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet
use: Structured process: model system, identify what can go wrong, choose mitigations, validate.
caveat: Depth should be proportional to exposure and risk.

title: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
use: Keep secrets out of source/logs and manage lifecycle/privilege appropriately.
caveat: Exact mechanism depends on environment/infrastructure.

title: OWASP Software Component Verification Standard (SCVS)
use: Component inventory, package management, analysis, provenance, and risk-based maturity.
caveat: Risk-acceptance criteria are organizational/business decisions; Koda must not invent legal/risk policy.

title: NIST NCCoE DevSecOps — Role of AI in software development
use: AI-generated content should be monitored/validated and supported by verifiable processes.
caveat: Project guidance evolves; use SSDF as the stable baseline.

title: Fu et al. — Security Weaknesses of Copilot-Generated Code in GitHub Projects
use: Supports independent verification of AI-generated code.
caveat: Model/tool/time/dataset-specific percentages must not be generalized.

title: DORA — Trunk-based development
use: Short-lived branches and frequent integration reduce integration burden.
caveat: Koda can still use feature worktrees; isolation does not require long-lived branches.

title: DORA — Continuous delivery
use: Keep software releasable; continuous delivery is distinct from automatic deployment.
caveat: Local/offline software may have no hosted deployment pipeline.

title: DORA — Version control
use: Version application, tests, build/deploy/config/migrations and relevant AI prompts/agent config.
caveat: Large binary artifacts may belong in artifact/blob storage rather than Git.

title: DORA — Code maintainability
use: Traceable dependencies and reproducible builds/installations support maintainability.
caveat: Does not prescribe one package manager or lock strategy.

title: Git — git-worktree documentation
use: Authoritative behavior for linked worktrees and lifecycle.
caveat: Worktrees are a Koda isolation mechanism, not a universal team branching policy.

title: GitHub Actions — Secure use reference
use: Full commit SHA is GitHub's immutable reference for third-party actions; secure workflow configuration.
caveat: GitHub-specific; update automation/policy may be needed.

title: GitHub — Dependency review
use: Can surface dependency vulnerabilities/licenses when platform capability is available.
caveat: Availability depends on repository type/plan/settings.

title: GitHub — CodeQL code scanning
use: CodeQL supports a defined language set and can identify vulnerabilities/errors.
caveat: Unsupported languages/frameworks require different tooling; platform/plan constraints apply.

title: SonarQube — About new code
use: Supports focusing quality improvement on changed/new code.
caveat: Sonar-specific methodology.

title: SonarQube — Quality gates
use: Quality gates are customizable and may differ across projects.
caveat: Built-in numeric defaults are vendor defaults, not universal engineering laws.

title: Microsoft Engineering Playbook — Observability recommended practices
use: Collect actionable failure/dependency/latency signals, start small, avoid sensitive logging.
caveat: Service-oriented; not every script/local app needs logs+metrics+traces.

title: Azure Well-Architected — Performance Efficiency principles
use: Use realistic performance targets, measurement, iterative optimization, and efficient resource use.
caveat: Cloud-oriented source; general measurement principle is broader.

title: Azure Architecture Center — Transient fault handling
use: Retry only likely transient faults; use bounded attempts, timeouts, backoff/jitter, and idempotency awareness.
caveat: Remote/distributed dependency context; not a reason to add retry frameworks to local computation.

title: DuckDB — Why DuckDB
use: DuckDB targets analytical/OLAP workloads and embedded simplicity; explicitly says no DB is one-size-fits-all.
caveat: Project source is authoritative about DuckDB, not other databases.

title: DuckDB — Concurrency
use: Documents process/write concurrency, optimistic conflicts, and current DuckLake/Quack options.
caveat: DuckDB is evolving rapidly; version/capability must be checked.

title: DuckDB — Environment / network-attached disks
use: Warns against native read-write DuckDB on NAS/NFS/SMB/Samba; read-only network storage differs.
caveat: Cloud block disks and lakehouse formats have different semantics.

title: DuckDB — Tuning Workloads
use: Analytical workload focus, profiling, memory caveats, remote I/O, connection reuse.
caveat: DuckDB-specific optimizations should not become universal DB rules.

title: SQLite — Appropriate Uses For SQLite
use: Client/server is preferable for many concurrent writers/direct network clients; embedded DB is strong for local low-write-concurrency use.
caveat: This research does not make SQLite Koda's default; it provides useful workload decision axes.

title: SQLite — SQLite Over a Network, Caveats and Considerations
use: Network filesystem locking/sync can be unreliable and may corrupt databases.
caveat: Filesystem implementation matters; client/server architecture avoids direct DB file sharing.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — Concurrency Control
use: PostgreSQL provides MVCC/locking/isolation for multiple concurrent sessions.
caveat: PostgreSQL is an example of client/server transactional architecture, not a universal database default.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — Backup and Restore
use: Different backup approaches carry tradeoffs; durable valuable data needs recovery planning.
caveat: Mechanisms are PostgreSQL-specific.

title: PostgreSQL 18 — ALTER TABLE
use: Schema changes may acquire strong locks; migration risk depends on operation/workload.
caveat: Exact behavior is PostgreSQL-specific.

title: Python Packaging — pyproject.toml specification
use: Canonical signal for Python build/project/tool configuration.
caveat: Legacy and tool-specific project layouts still exist.

title: Python Packaging — pylock.toml specification
use: Standards-based lock-file semantics.
caveat: Python currently has multiple lock mechanisms; Koda must preserve existing tool choice.

title: npm — package-lock.json
use: Exact dependency tree/reproducible npm installs and source-controlled lock state.
caveat: pnpm/yarn/bun use different lock formats.

title: Maven — Build Lifecycle
use: Use configured native lifecycle before inventing bespoke commands.
caveat: Project plugins may extend/change behavior.

title: Maven — Reproducible Builds
use: Reproducible artifacts are a deliberate build property and can be verified.
caveat: Bit-for-bit reproducibility may need plugin/environment work.

title: TypeScript — strict TSConfig option
use: Strict mode gives stronger type-checking guarantees.
caveat: Enabling it in an existing project can be a migration; preserve project policy.

title: Rust Cargo — cargo test
use: Use native project test lifecycle.
caveat: Projects may define extra checks.

title: Rust Clippy — Usage
use: Clippy provides configurable lint levels; allowances can be deliberate.
caveat: Do not turn all optional lints into hard failures.

title: Go — Modules Reference
use: Detect module/workspace state and use native lifecycle.
caveat: Multi-module workspaces require `go.work` awareness.

title: .NET CLI — dotnet test
use: Use native solution/project test lifecycle.
caveat: Runner/config differ across SDK/project.

title: Gradle — Testing in Java/JVM projects
use: Use existing test/check lifecycle and configured suites.
caveat: Builds can define custom tasks/suites.

title: Nx — Affected tasks
use: Reuse existing affected/project-graph tooling to scope checks.
caveat: Shared lock/config changes may broaden impact.

title: W3C — Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
use: Testable accessibility criteria for web UI.
caveat: Applicable primarily to web content; legal obligations vary.

title: W3C — Using ARIA
use: Prefer native HTML semantics and preserve keyboard interaction.
caveat: Custom widgets may legitimately require ARIA.

title: GOV.UK Service Manual — Start by learning user needs
use: Focus on the user's problem/outcome and use language they recognize.
caveat: Government-service context; principles should later be tested with Koda users.

title: GOV.UK Service Manual — Designing good questions
use: Ask only needed information and use understandable language.
caveat: Service-form context; use the principle, not form-specific UI.

title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
use: If a project declares SemVer, incompatible public API changes map to major releases and compatible additions/fixes to minor/patch semantics.
caveat: SemVer applies only when the project defines a public API and chooses SemVer; Koda must not force it on every project.

title: Microsoft REST API Guidelines
use: Existing services should not receive breaking changes merely to comply with newer guidelines; breaking API changes require explicit versioning policy.
caveat: Microsoft conventions are not a universal REST standard; the compatibility principle generalizes better than exact version mechanics.

title: GitHub REST API — Breaking changes
use: Concrete examples of breaking vs additive changes and explicit supported-version migration.
caveat: GitHub-specific API contract; exact support windows are not universal.

title: Kubernetes Deprecation Policy
use: Stable APIs require explicit compatibility/deprecation discipline and versioned removal.
caveat: Kubernetes timelines/tracks are project-specific, not Koda defaults.

title: SLSA v1.2 — Build requirements
use: Build provenance identifies artifact outputs and how they were produced; stronger levels add integrity guarantees.
caveat: Intended for produced/distributed artifacts and supply-chain assurance; not every local script needs SLSA provenance.

title: CycloneDX Specification Overview
use: Machine-readable representation of components, dependencies, services and related software supply-chain information.
caveat: An SBOM describes inventory/transparency; it is not itself build provenance or proof that components are safe.

title: GitHub — Artifact attestations
use: Signed attestations can establish where/how GitHub-built artifacts were produced.
caveat: Availability differs by GitHub plan/repository visibility; not a universal requirement.

title: OpenSSF Scorecard — Checks documentation
use: Pinning, token permissions, update tools and vulnerability checks have distinct tradeoffs; least-privilege CI tokens matter.
caveat: Scorecard scoring is a tool heuristic, not a universal Koda quality score.

title: GitHub — OpenID Connect reference
use: OIDC enables workflows to obtain short-lived tokens rather than relying solely on stored long-lived cloud credentials.
caveat: Only relevant when GitHub Actions authenticates to compatible external services.

title: GitHub Actions — Secure use reference
use: Least privilege, secrets handling, third-party action risk, and safe handling of untrusted values in workflows.
caveat: GitHub Actions-specific.

title: GitHub Actions — Script injections
use: Repository/PR metadata can be attacker-controlled and must not be interpolated directly into executable scripts.
caveat: GitHub Actions-specific manifestation of a general untrusted-input principle.

title: OWASP CI/CD Security Cheat Sheet
use: CI/CD is privileged infrastructure; least privilege, pipeline integrity, secret hygiene, dependency-chain and poisoned-pipeline risks matter.
caveat: Exact mitigations depend on the CI platform and threat model.

title: CISA et al. — Shifting the Balance of Cybersecurity Risk: Secure by Design and Default
use: Secure configuration should be the default and security complexity should not be pushed onto customers.
caveat: Product-manufacturer guidance; exact controls depend on product surface.

title: CISA — Eliminating Buffer Overflow Vulnerabilities
use: Where feasible, memory-safe languages and safer toolchains reduce entire classes of memory-safety defects, especially in new/high-risk code.
caveat: Does not justify rewriting every existing C/C++ codebase or choosing a low-level memory-safe language for unrelated application work.

title: CISA/FBI — Product Security Bad Practices update
use: Prioritize secure design, reduce known defect classes, and avoid shifting security burden to customers.
caveat: Originally aimed at products supporting critical infrastructure; broader applicability should remain risk-proportional.

title: The Twelve-Factor App — Config
use: Separates deploy-varying configuration/credentials from source code.
caveat: Environment variables are not a universal mechanism for desktop/local/embedded software; use the separation principle, not dogma.

title: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet
use: Validate untrusted data early, syntactically and semantically; prefer trusted/server-side enforcement and framework validators.
caveat: Allowlisting is strongest for structured/fixed inputs; free-form text requires more nuanced validation.

title: OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
use: Logs should avoid secrets/sensitive data, remain useful, and be protected from tampering/abuse.
caveat: Logging volume/content is operationally and legally context-dependent.

title: OWASP Database Security Cheat Sheet
use: Database identities should use least privilege; credentials must not be hard-coded; backup/security configuration matters.
caveat: Specific permission granularity and storage mechanisms differ by database/environment.

title: PostgreSQL — Transactions
use: Multi-step changes can be committed or rolled back as a unit.
caveat: PostgreSQL mechanics are specific; transactional concepts generalize to capable stores.

title: PostgreSQL — Constraints
use: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, PK, FK and CHECK-like constraints can enforce invariants at the datastore boundary.
caveat: Exact constraint features/performance differ by database.

title: Azure Architecture Center — Asynchronous Messaging Options
use: Duplicate delivery is a real distributed-system concern; consumers often need idempotent handling.
caveat: Only relevant when asynchronous messaging/at-least-once delivery exists.

title: Azure Architecture Center — Microservices Assessment and Readiness
use: Microservices require business, organizational, infrastructure, deployment, testing and operational readiness; gaps should be prioritized by impact.
caveat: Azure/cloud perspective; use the readiness/tradeoff principle rather than Azure-specific platform choices.

title: Azure Architecture Center — Microservices architecture style
use: Microservices increase system-wide complexity, distributed consistency/testing/communication and governance burden.
caveat: Does not mean monoliths are always preferable.

title: Azure Architecture Center — Cache-Aside Pattern
use: Caching introduces expiration, consistency, invalidation, capacity and multi-instance behavior that must be justified by access patterns.
caveat: Azure examples are implementation-specific; caching tradeoffs generalize.

title: Microsoft Research — Principles of Eventual Consistency
use: Eventual consistency is a deliberate semantic tradeoff, not a free scalability feature.
caveat: Formal distributed-systems context; most simple applications should avoid introducing such complexity without need.

title: Cargo Book — Cargo.toml vs Cargo.lock
scope: Dependency manifest vs resolved lock state
use: Manifest constraints and exact resolved lock state serve different purposes.
caveat: Rust-specific; other ecosystems differ.

title: Cargo Book — FAQ: Cargo.lock in version control
use: Lockfile needs differ by package role; deterministic end products and reusable libraries have different dependency-resolution concerns.
caveat: Rust-specific evidence supporting a broader 'preserve ecosystem semantics' rule.

title: Python Packaging — Dependency specifiers
use: Python package dependencies may intentionally express version ranges, markers, extras or exact artifacts rather than one universal pin style.
caveat: Does not by itself prescribe application lock strategy.

title: OpenSSF Scorecard — Beginner checks
use: Pinned dependencies should be paired with a process/tool for updates; token permissions should be least-privilege.
caveat: OpenSSF scoring/remediation is guidance, not a universal project score.

title: CISA — Secure by Demand Guide
use: SBOMs and vulnerability-class elimination are useful product/security evidence; secure building blocks reduce user/developer burden.
caveat: Procurement/product guidance; not every internal tool needs a formal SBOM.

title: Azure Architecture Center — Retry Pattern
use: Retries need exception classification, bounded policy and idempotency awareness.
caveat: Remote/transient failures only.

title: AWS Prescriptive Guidance — Transactional outbox pattern
use: When a database update must reliably result in an event, naive dual writes can fail; transactional outbox and idempotent consumers are one applicable pattern.
caveat: Only applies to event-driven dual-write problems; do not add an outbox to ordinary CRUD apps.

title: GitHub Actions — Script injection security
use: Untrusted PR/issue/branch metadata can become command injection when interpolated into generated scripts.
caveat: GitHub Actions-specific implementation.

title: Liquibase — Expand-Contract Pattern
use: For rolling/zero-downtime systems, breaking schema changes can be decomposed into additive/migrate/remove phases.
caveat: Vendor pattern guidance; only necessary when old/new application versions overlap or downtime must be avoided.

title: CycloneDX — Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX)
use: Distinguishes a vulnerable component finding from whether the specific product context is actually affected/exploitable.
caveat: VEX statements require trustworthy evidence; Koda must not manufacture 'not affected' claims.

title: OpenVEX Specification
authority: Community specification aligned to CISA VEX requirements
use: Shows vulnerability status is product-contextual and can represent fixed/not-affected/investigating states.
caveat: OpenVEX is a draft/community format; do not require it universally.

title: GitHub — Configure dependency review action
use: Dependency review thresholds are configurable by vulnerability severity/scope and can enforce organization-specific license policy.
caveat: GitHub-specific and license acceptability is policy/legal context, not Koda judgment.
